title: Maximum Number of Words You Can Type
statement: Some letter keys on a keyboard are dead, and every other key still works. `text` holds words of lowercase letters, with exactly one space between neighbouring words and no space at the start or end. `brokenLetters` lists the dead keys, and no letter appears in it twice (it may be empty). A word can be typed in full only if none of its letters is a dead key. Return how many words of `text` can be typed in full.
constraints: text is words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space
Each word contains only lowercase English letters
brokenLetters contains distinct lowercase English letters

tests.name: Test 4
input: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

tests.name: Test 6
input: x y z x y z

notes:
## Intuition

A word is typeable exactly when none of its letters is a dead key, so each word can be judged on its own. The only repeated question is "is this letter broken?", and a set of the broken letters answers it in constant time. A slower but equally correct idea scans `brokenLetters` for every letter of the text; with at most 26 dead keys that is still fine, but the set makes the intent clearer.

## Approach

1. Put every letter of `brokenLetters` into a set `broken`; start `count` at 0.
2. Split `text` on single spaces and take each `word` in turn.
3. Assume the word is `typeable`, then look at each `letter`. If the letter is in `broken`, mark the word as not typeable and stop scanning it.
4. If the word survived the scan, add one to `count`.
5. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "hello world"`, `brokenLetters = "ad"`, so `broken = {a, d}`.

- `"hello"`: none of h, e, l, l, o is in the set, so `count` becomes 1.
- `"world"`: w, o, r and l pass, but `d` is broken, so the word is skipped.

The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + b), where n is `text.length` and b is `brokenLetters.length`: each character is checked once with a constant-time set lookup.
- Space: O(n + b): the split words plus a set of at most 26 letters.

## Pitfalls

- `brokenLetters` can be empty; then every word counts.
- Stop scanning a word at its first dead key, but do not stop the outer loop: later words still need checking.
- Count words, not characters: one bad letter rules out its whole word, however long it is.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `broken` | set of the dead letter keys |
| `count` | number of fully typeable words so far |
| `word` | the word being checked |
| `typeable` | whether `word` has avoided every dead key so far |
| `letter` | the current letter of `word` |

narration.12: Did the word get through every letter?
narration.13: Then it can be typed, so count it.
narration.16: Every word has been judged; return how many can be typed.
